findings.title: The `[codex]` in the install hint and marker is swallowed by Rich on every surface that prints it
findings.description:
The hint `pip install 'squadron-ai[codex]'` and the marker `(needs [codex] extra)` (line 173) reach the terminal through Rich markup strings. Rich treats `[codex]` as a style tag and drops it, so the user sees `pip install 'squadron-ai'` and `(needs  extra)`.
- `src/squadron/cli/commands/review.py:734` interpolates the exception into `rprint(f"[red]Error: Review failed — {exc}[/red]")`.
- `src/squadron/cli/commands/doctor.py:78` interpolates `fix_hint` into `[dim]fix: …[/dim]`.
- `src/squadron/cli/commands/setup.py:72` interpolates the step command into `[bold]$ …[/bold]`.
- `src/squadron/cli/commands/models.py:113` passes plain strings to `table.add_row`, which renders markup.
- `src/squadron/cli/commands/auth.py:36` prints `setup_hint` through `rprint`.

Only `run.py` and `run_dry_run.py` call `escape()` today. The design must require escaping at each of these sites and a test that asserts the literal `[codex]` in rendered output. Without it, Value line 28 and functional requirement line 190 are unmet.

findings.title: `pip install 'squadron-ai[codex]'` does not fix the documented install methods
findings.description: `README.md:41-44` documents `uv tool install squadron-ai` and `pipx install squadron-ai`. Under either, ambient `pip install` targets a different environment (a uv tool venv has no pip), and `sq` keeps failing with the same message. The walkthrough (line 209) only exercises a hand-made venv. The hint should name `uv tool install 'squadron-ai[codex]'` and the pipx equivalent, or the "exact command" requirement is unmet for most users.

findings.title: `create_agent` ordering is unspecified; as coded, a not-logged-in user never sees the install hint
findings.description:
`src/squadron/providers/codex/provider.py:32-34` raises `ProviderAuthError("No Codex credentials found. …")` before any runtime check. The Data Flow shows only `create_agent → resolve_codex_runtime()`.
- If the credential check stays first, walkthrough step 1 (line 210, fresh venv, no login) and requirement line 190 fail: the user is told to authenticate, not to install.
- If the runtime check moves first, `tests/providers/codex/test_provider.py:79-88` (`pytest.raises(ProviderAuthError, match="No Codex credentials")`) fails in CI, where the extra is absent.

The design must state the order and name the test change.

findings.title: Existing guidance keeps sending users to the Codex CLI and npm
findings.description:
`setup_hint` (`src/squadron/providers/codex/auth.py:64`, "Run 'codex' CLI to authenticate, or set OPENAI_API_KEY") is changed only in the fallback's "fails" outcome. In the "works" outcome it still names a binary the bundled install does not put on PATH, and it feeds `provider.py:34`, `auth.py:36,57` and `doctor_checks.py:233`. The design updates the README only (line 174) and leaves these stale:
- `src/squadron/cli/commands/setup_steps.py:138-141` ("The Codex CLI enables the codex provider") and its "Install Codex CLI" step.
- `docs/QUICKSTART.md:126,136-140` (`npm i -g @openai/codex`, `codex auth login`), plus its link to `README.md#using-codex-experimental`, which breaks if that heading changes.
- `src/squadron/providers/profiles.py:86` (description "(MCP)").

This contradicts the "no npm" value at line 25.

findings.title: D9's per-alias provider resolution breaks an existing model-list test and has no error handling
findings.description: `sq models` never resolves profiles today. `tests/cli/test_model_list.py:479-485` pins that an alias with profile `some-custom-profile` is listed with exit 0. Under D9 that alias reaches `get_profile` (KeyError, `profiles.py:168-170`) or `get_provider` (KeyError, `registry.py:22-24`, after `loader.py:23-24` swallows the ImportError). A malformed `providers.toml` would newly break the listing too. The design must say that an unresolvable profile or provider yields no marker and no error. It also makes a list command import the `sdk` and `openai` provider packages.

findings.title: `applies_effort=True` fails a pinned test the design does not name
findings.description: `tests/review/test_review_client.py:1544-1558` (`test_codex_artifact_has_no_effort_key`) takes `CodexProvider().capabilities` and asserts `result.effort is None` and `"- Effort: backend default"`. It fails once the capability flips. The class docstring at `tests/providers/test_capabilities.py:51` and the comments at `review/models.py:245` and `review_client.py:258-262` state the old behavior. Line 204 promises the full existing suite passes; this test must be listed as changed.

findings.title: D8's empty-response error bypasses the existing `EmptyFinalTurnError` recovery path
findings.description: `src/squadron/providers/errors.py:34-54` already defines `EmptyFinalTurnError` for exactly this case. `review_client.py:370-386` catches it and sends one recovery turn on the same agent. D8 raises a plain `ProviderError`, so a Codex empty turn fails the review outright, although `CodexAgent` reuses its thread and could take the recovery turn. The existing error also requires integer `reasoning_chars`, `tool_calls_made` and `failed_tool_calls`, which Codex cannot supply without fabricating zeros. The design must either use it and say what it passes, or state that Codex opts out of recovery.

findings.title: The failure table collapses every error to plain `ProviderError`, ignoring subclasses that callers branch on
findings.description:
- **Not logged in / token rejected:** specified as `ProviderError`. `src/squadron/server/routes/agents.py:67-75` maps `ProviderAuthError` to 401 and everything else to 502, and `create_agent` already raises `ProviderAuthError` for the same condition.
- **Rate-limited:** specified as `ProviderError`. `src/squadron/metrology/audit.py:699` catches `ProviderRateLimitError` to pause a campaign.
- **Timeout:** specified as `ProviderError`. `ProviderTimeoutError` exists and the OpenAI agent uses it.

The row at line 131 also gives no way to tell an auth `CodexRpcError` from any other RPC error.

findings.title: Timeout and cancellation mid-turn: interrupt mechanism and post-timeout agent state are not defined
findings.description:
The rows say "cancel the turn" and "turn handle interrupted". Interfaces Required (line 54) lists only `AsyncThread.run(...)` returning `TurnResult`, with no turn handle or interrupt call. Whether cancelling the await stops the runtime's turn is not established.

The `_codex`/`_thread` reset is specified only for `TransportClosedError` (line 129). After a timeout the agent keeps a thread that may still be running a turn.

"`shutdown()` still runs in `finally`" holds for `review_client.py:281-282` and `pipeline/summary_oneshot.py:169-170`. It does not hold for daemon-held agents (`core/agent_registry.py:49,118`), which stay registered and receive the next message on that thread. The design should reset or close the client on timeout.

findings.title: D6 rests on an unverified reading of `usage.last` and leaves `turns` undefined
findings.description:
The design asserts "`last` = this turn" (line 54). I could not check this. In the upstream Codex protocol as I recall it, `last` is the most recent model response, which would under-report an agentic turn that makes many requests. The design should pin the semantics with the real-types or real-run test, or derive per-turn usage from the `total` delta.

It also says to stamp `metadata["turns"]` (line 55) without a value. `core/usage.py:49-57` and `review/turn_capture.py:84-86` define `turns` as requests sent. A hard-coded 1 would be the fabricated plausible value that `turn_capture.py:69-70` forbids. Either leave it unstamped or define it.

findings.title: The `OPENAI_API_KEY` fallback's "works" branch is not carried through the new status, logout and login flows
findings.description:
If the fallback is kept:
- **Status:** line 86 runs `account()` for any valid `InteractiveLogin` strategy, so a key-only environment spawns the runtime on every `sq auth status`. What `account_summary()` returns when `account.root` is not a `ChatgptAccount` is unspecified.
- **Logout:** walkthrough step 8 (line 219) expects `✗ not authenticated`. With the key exported (step 6 uses `env -u OPENAI_API_KEY`, implying it usually is) the row reads `✓ authenticated | OPENAI_API_KEY`.
- **Login:** `sq auth login openai-oauth` with a valid key today prints "authenticated (OPENAI_API_KEY)". Whether it now always opens the browser is unstated.
- **Tests:** `tests/cli/test_auth.py:66-74` sets `OPENAI_API_KEY`. In an environment with the extra installed it would spawn the real runtime, unless status is specified to skip `account()` when the source is not the auth file.

findings.title: `sq auth status` with a login file present but the extra absent is unhandled
findings.description: Validity is file presence, so a user who logged in with the Codex CLI and never installed the extra is "valid". Status then calls `account_summary()`, and `resolve_codex_runtime()` raises a `ProviderError`. The row covers only "timeout or SDK error". As written this either aborts the whole table (violating "never … block the other profiles' rows") or logs a WARNING on every run. The design should specify no `account()` call and no warning when the runtime is unresolvable.

findings.title: Validity is a hard-coded file path while login is owned by the runtime
findings.description: `src/squadron/providers/codex/auth.py:17-18` fixes `~/.codex/auth.json`. The design is itself unsure whether the runtime honors a `CODEX_HOME`-style location (line 232), and nothing establishes that the runtime always stores credentials in that file. If either differs, `sq auth login` reports success, status says not authenticated, and `create_agent` refuses with `ProviderAuthError`. The user can only escape by editing environment or files. The login flow already re-reads `account()` (line 84); the design should say what happens when that succeeds but the file is absent.

findings.title: No hang bound for logout, or for runtime start and login initiation
findings.description: `codex.login_timeout_s` bounds only `handle.wait()`. `codex.account_timeout_s` bounds status and post-login confirmation. `sq auth logout` (runtime start plus `logout()`) and the pre-`wait()` part of login (runtime start plus `login_chatgpt()`) have no row and no timeout, although line 82 lists both as spawn sites. A hung runtime blocks the command indefinitely.

findings.title: Generic auth CLI must read a Codex-named config key to satisfy `InteractiveLogin.login`
findings.description: `login(..., timeout: float, ...)` is required. The default is `codex.login_timeout_s`, which `--timeout` overrides (line 108). So `cli/commands/auth.py` must read a `codex.*` key for whichever strategy implements the Protocol. That is the provider-identity coupling D3 and line 198 set out to avoid. `account_summary()` takes no timeout, so the two bounds would also live in different layers. Make `timeout` `float | None` and let the strategy resolve its own default.

findings.title: `pyright clean` and the drift test have no environment in which they hold
findings.description:
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:33` runs `uv sync --dev` with no extras, so the real-types test (line 200) is skipped on every leg. "A drifted SDK surface fails loudly" never executes.
- `pyproject.toml:94-98` sets strict mode with `reportMissingImports = true`. The new `login.py` uses SDK types and fails pyright in that environment unless it is suppressed into `Unknown`s.
- `pyproject.toml:95` excludes `providers/codex/agent.py` from pyright, so "pyright clean" says nothing about the port.

The design must state whether CI gains a leg with the extra (keeping one without, for line 204) and how the pyright exclude changes.

findings.title: Walkthrough steps that do not run as written
findings.description:
- `sq model list` (lines 37, 73, 173, 205, 211) is not a command. `src/squadron/cli/app.py:55` registers `models`, so it is `sq models list`.
- Step 1's "`sq doctor` → `codex provider` row WARN" shows nothing. `doctor.py:64-65` hides WARN rows without `-v`.
- Step 2's row status for "installed, not logged in" is never defined. If it is WARN it is hidden too.

findings.title: The doctor row and `ExtraRequirement` are specified inconsistently
findings.description:
- `missing_extra_hint()` uses `resolve_codex_runtime()`, which raises `ProviderError` both for "package missing" and "no binary" (line 80). Nothing lets the caller tell them apart, so a no-binary state would be labelled as needing the extra.
- The row shows "package version", but `CodexRuntime` is `(source, path|None)` (line 63) and doctor is forbidden its own probing.
- The mapping from row state to `CheckStatus` is absent.
- `run_all_checks` feeds `sq setup` (`setup_steps.py:216-266`). A new WARN row becomes an optional setup step printing the pip command, with no `_EXPLANATION` or `_TITLE_MAP` entry. The design does not mention setup.

findings.title: Smaller inaccuracies and ordering
findings.description:
- `get_provider("openai-oauth")` does not raise the install hint. `registry.py:16-25` returns the provider or raises KeyError; `create_agent` raises the hint.
- The hedges at lines 25 and 171 about the distribution name are resolvable now: `pyproject.toml:2` is `squadron-ai`.
- D9 appears before D8.
- The "Codex Turn" failure table also holds login and status rows.

findings.title: Deferred slice 907 specifies a conflicting `codex` extra
findings.description: `project-documents/user/slices/907-slice.optional-dependency-split-serve-and-codex-extras.md:40-44,102-119` (status deferred) defines an intentionally empty `codex = []` extra and an npm-hint binary guard. This design supersedes both. 907 should be annotated so it is not later implemented as written.

findings.title: Proportionality: sized to the plan entry, with two small cuts available
findings.description: The mechanisms map to plan requirements, and timeouts as config keys follow the `cf.mcp_timeout_s` precedent. `--timeout` duplicates `codex.login_timeout_s` and nothing requires both. The "reusable by any later Codex-adjacent feature" framing (line 181) is speculative but adds no work.
